rules.title: Protect event logs from unauthorised access, modification or deletion, including by encrypting them during transit and at rest and securing the systems and accounts used to store, manage and analyse them.
Forward high-value, security-relevant event logs and configuration changes from infrastructure, operating systems and applications to a central log storage capability.
Establish a centralised event log storage capability that protects logs from unauthorised access or modification.
Ensure event logs are normalised, time-synchronised and enriched to support correlation across systems and environments.
Ensure detection logic identifies unauthorised changes, anomalous authentication activity and suspicious software execution.
Triage alerts and events in a timely manner to determine whether cyber security incident thresholds have been met.
Use indicators from across identities, applications, data and infrastructure activity rather than isolated signals when identifying cyber security incidents.
Continuously monitor and analyse software execution behaviour on systems to detect where legitimate tools and utilities are being used for malicious purposes.
Review detection coverage periodically to identify gaps arising from new assets, services or architectural changes.

Formally define and establish executive and board-level accountabilities for cyber security, including setting, monitoring and adjusting organisational risk appetite, and review these accountabilities at a defined cadence.
Establish and maintain an approved risk management methodology and plan that is used to assess and treat cyber security risks.

Assign sufficient cyber security personnel and resources with the required skills to operate, monitor, maintain and manage the lifecycle of security controls and define cyber security responsibilities within role descriptions.
Periodically review cyber security resourcing against cyber threat trends, cyber security incident outcomes and organisational changes.
Establish and maintain executive accountability for the use, governance and risk management of artificial intelligence within the organisation.

Select and engage suppliers of software, hardware and services on the basis of a cyber supply chain risk assessment proportionate to the risk the supplier introduces, and retain appropriate assurance evidence to support the decision.
Maintain current assurance that suppliers continue to meet their cyber security commitments, and act when that assurance lapses or the supplier’s risk changes.

Establish and maintain a process for identifying, assessing and treating cyber security risks associated with legacy systems and unsupported technologies through compensating controls, enhanced monitoring and assurance until the systems can be removed or replaced.
Use an approved asset inventory mechanism that supports automated discovery to detect new and changed physical and non-physical assets.
Maintain current records of infrastructure, operating systems, applications, identities, credentials and data assets.
Identify relevant weaknesses, malicious actor techniques and cyber threat behaviours when undertaking risk assessments and review these inputs on a continuous basis.
Design systems securely to provide visibility, enforce authorised access, protect data, minimise required and default privileges, limit exposed services and remove unnecessary functionality.
Secure build and deployment processes to enforce controls consistently across systems.

Define approved configuration baselines, informed by vendor and industry hardening guidance, that disable or remove unnecessary services, insecure settings, and unsupported or weak communication protocols.
Deploy approved configuration baselines on systems, including infrastructure, operating systems and applications.
Detect and respond to configuration drift using scheduled technical assessments and, where supported, automated monitoring, based on system criticality and change rate.
Ensure administrative activities can only be performed from dedicated and hardened environments that are isolated from unprivileged user workloads.
Enforce explicit session establishment controls before privileged actions are permitted, including the use of time-bound privilege grants.
Record all administrative or management actions that modify systems, configurations or controls, including the details of the associated user, timestamp and target.
Identify known software and configuration weaknesses of assets through continuous and repeatable assessment activities, including vulnerability scanning activities.
Apply security patches or updates within defined risk-based timeframes or automatically where operational impact is low.

Remediate or mitigate vulnerabilities exceeding defined risk thresholds within defined timeframes based on exploitation, exposure, criticality, impact and compensating controls, and verify treatment effectiveness.
Permit only supported, verified and organisation-authorised software to execute on systems, with exceptions minimised, formally risk accepted, time-bound, monitored and regularly reviewed.
Restrict administrative and management tooling to approved software sets and executed from only authorised, known locations.
Inspect outbound content flows to detect unauthorised transfer of sensitive or high-value data.
Block outbound network connections to known malicious or untrusted destinations.
Inspect inbound content from external or untrusted sources to prevent delivery of malicious or unsafe content.
Back up important data, applications and settings on a defined schedule to secure, resilient storage protected by encryption and immutable, offline, logically isolated or equivalent controls.
Isolate backup repositories from general user environments and production workloads, ensuring they are separated from primary systems to prevent unauthorised access, modification or deletion.
Conduct regular testing of backup and restoration procedures to ensure that backups are reliable and capable of meeting defined recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives.
Periodically review and update access privileges in alignment with current roles, duties and business requirements.
Grant only authorised administrative roles permissions to create, modify or delete accounts and roles, and access privileged functions or applications.
Provision user, administrative and non-person accounts with only the minimum access and privileges required to perform defined operational functions.

section_path: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management
rules.title: Identify and disable or remove default and unused accounts regularly, permitting exceptions only where the account is documented, justified, hardened and monitored.

section_path: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management
rules.title: Store authentication keys, secrets and tokens in approved secure repositories with access controls, including MFA.

section_path: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management
rules.title: Identify and remediate unsecured keys, secrets and credentials by regularly scanning codebases, configuration files, file shares and user collaboration platforms.

section_path: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management
rules.title: Use phishing-resistant MFA for users authenticating to systems, including from untrusted, external or high-risk locations.

section_path: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management
rules.title: Disable legacy authentication protocols or, where this is not feasible, restrict and monitor their use, apply compensating controls and establish a time-bound decommissioning plan.

section_path: PRO-13 - Identity, credential and access management
rules.title: Ensure that user, machine, system and service account credentials are unique per system or account, particularly in high-privilege contexts.

Ensure all personnel receive cyber security awareness training, that is tailored to how they will interact with systems, applications and data in their assigned roles, before being granted access to organisational systems and data.
Update and provide cyber security awareness training on a regular basis to reflect current threats and operational considerations.
Assess the integrity and authenticity of software, components and updates before use, and verify provenance where suitable supplier evidence is available.
Use vendor advisories and threat intelligence to maintain awareness of supplier, product and component exposure to compromise, and act within timeframes proportionate to the risk.
Isolate systems within network zones based on business criticality and trust level, and restrict and monitor inbound and outbound access to explicitly approved pathways and services.
Limit lateral movement between, and within, network segments to explicitly approved pathways and services, based on business requirements and trust levels.
Use documented, tested and approved cyber security incident response procedures when responding to cyber security incidents.
Perform post-cyber security incident reviews to identify the security gaps that enabled each stage of the cyber security incident.
Evaluate the monitoring coverage and cyber security incident response procedures following cyber security incidents.
Integrate external coordination obligations into cyber security incident response activities where required.
